#2724. Texas A&M stock report, from Saturday's loss to South Carolina

Texas A&M suffered another frustrating SEC road loss Saturday, falling 17-9 to No. 21 South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium despite outgaining the Gamecocks and controlling much of the contest.

The Aggies entered the fourth quarter leading 9-7 but failed to protect their advantage as South Carolina scored 10 unanswered points. Texas A&M dropped to 4-5 overall and 1-5 in SEC play, leaving the team needing two victories in its final three games to become bowl eligible.

Offensive production wasn't the issue, as the Aggies finished with 457 total yards, including 206 rushing yards, while recording 26 first downs. However, missed opportunities, penalties and an inability to finish drives prevented Texas A&M from reaching the end zone.

Several individual performances offered encouragement, particularly in the running game and on defense. Still, the Aggies couldn't turn those efforts into a victory, continuing a troubling pattern against SEC competition.

Here is whose stock rose and fell against South Carolina.

Owens delivered his most productive rushing performance of the season, consistently finding lanes and giving Texas A&M explosive plays. His 44-yard run highlighted an impressive afternoon, but the Aggies couldn't capitalize on his production with a touchdown. Owens averaged more than seven yards per carry and accounted for most of the team's rushing offense.

Stats: 19 carries, 137 yards, 7.2 yards per carry.

Ratcliffe helped anchor a defensive effort that kept South Carolina's offense in check for much of the afternoon. The senior safety contributed in coverage and against the run, helping limit the Gamecocks to just four third-down conversions. His performance was one of the more encouraging aspects of another difficult road loss.

Stats: Six tackles, one pass breakup, one quarterback hurry.

White remained one of Texas A&M's most dependable special teams contributors, delivering another outstanding performance against South Carolina. The senior punter averaged 51.2 yards on four attempts, placing all four punts inside the Gamecocks' 20-yard line without recording a touchback. His longest punt traveled 55 yards, and his ability to flip field position helped keep the Aggies competitive despite their offensive struggles.

Stats: Four punts, 205 yards, 51.2 yards per punt, four inside the 20, long of 55 yards.

Reed completed 25 passes without throwing an interception, but the passing attack struggled to generate touchdowns. Despite throwing for 251 yards, Reed couldn't consistently finish drives, and Texas A&M's offense failed to score a touchdown for the third time in SEC play. The quarterback also struggled to make an impact as a runner.

Stats: 25-of-43 passing, 251 yards, zero touchdowns, zero interceptions / nine carries, eight yards.

Horton led Texas A&M with 78 receiving yards, but his costly drops overshadowed an otherwise productive afternoon. With the Aggies leading 9-7 in the third quarter, Horton dropped a potential touchdown pass on first-and-goal, beginning a disastrous sequence that ended with a missed field goal. He also dropped two passes in the fourth quarter that could have extended drives. Despite leading the team in receiving, Horton's inability to make critical catches contributed to Texas A&M's failure to reach the end zone.

Stats: Five receptions, 78 yards, zero touchdowns, 10 targets.

Texas A&M moved the football effectively between the 20-yard lines but repeatedly failed to finish scoring opportunities. Penalties near the goal line and missed chances forced the Aggies to settle for field goals instead of touchdowns. The inability to capitalize on promising drives ultimately overshadowed an otherwise productive statistical performance.

Stats: One score in three red-zone trips / zero touchdowns / 457 total yards.

That shouldn't have happened. On a night the Brooklyn Nets out-rebounded the Atlanta Hawks by 13, it was their inability to grab rebounds in the final two minutes that lost them the game. Brooklyn wound up losing 124-121 Saturday night, letting a game slip away that was there for the taking.

Back-to-backs are tough, and going from Atlanta to Dallas is especially challenging. We'll see how the Nets do in this one.

If they want to win, they'll need to slow down an old friend. Kyrie Irving is back after missing last year with an ACL tear. He's averaging 21 points a night while his shooting numbers remain strong, the way he's getting his buckets looks a little different than what we're used to.

His field goal attempts share of field-goal attempts inside of three feet is at the lowest mark of his career, while his three-point rate is at a career high. Chances are that'll change the further he gets away from the injury, but it's certainly something to keep an eye on. Either way, Irving remains a magnetic scorer and a blast to watch when his game is on.

He didn't play in the fourth quarter, and with Brown Jr. out tonight Sunday, Traoré should get all the minutes he can handle. When Brown Jr. returns, we'll see if the coaching staff finally starts to give the young guards more playing time alongside each other. The Nets have little to lose by giving that pairing a longer look. Why not give it a shot?

We'll see if the Nets can be great on the glass for all 48 minutes tonight. Brooklyn did great for most of the night, but gave away possessions late with their inability to secure the rebound. Day'ron Sharpe and the team will look to keep Daniel Gafford, Morez Johnson, and the rest of the Mavs off the glass.

Speaking of Sharpe, the big guy collected the first triple-double of his career with 12 points, ten rebounds, and a career high 13 assists.

I try not to fall for hyperbole, but I think I'm gonna make an exception here. Something that will come with time and experience is the ability to make an impact at the end of games. "This is not to say that Flagg is incapable. We have seen him take over fourth quarters multiple times this year. It is his job to take the pressure off Irving late in games. He's young, so it is entirely possible he was in his own head after a poor shooting game. But learning to be the guy on a nightly basis and flushing the bad performances will be the next step in his evolution."

And that next step is gonna be a doozy. That said, he's been terrific already and it'll be exciting to watch him ball out tonight.

#2721. Recap: Lions’ defense dominates in 19-9 win over Dolphins

The Detroit Lions offense has failed to score more than 20 points in three straight weeks, but the defense has carried them to wins in all three of those games.

It was the same story in the Lions' Week 9 win over the Miami Dolphins. The offense was disjointed and had to overcome some poor offensive line play early. And while they eventually were able to find some success late, Detroit's defensive performance is what really stood out.

The Lions held the Dolphins to just 77 yards rushing and 3.7 yards per carry. Miami quarterback Malik Willis had just 128 passing yards. And, most importantly, the Lions held the Dolphins out of the end zone completely for all four quarters.

It was an inspired performance, particularly without the heartbeat of the defense, Jack Campbell. The Lions clearly dedicated the game to him, sporting No. 46 jerseys while walking into the stadium. And while Campbell vowed this week to eventually continue his NFL career, Detroit proved on Sunday that they can operate without him for now.

Here's a full recap of the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins.

The Lions got the ball first and had great field position after the kickoff landed before the landing zone. Interestingly, it was Miles Frazier at left guard to start the game in place of the (presumably) healthy Christian Mahogany. After picking up 6 yards on the first two plays, Jared Goff and the Lions faced an quick third-and-4. Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown for a nice gain of 16 yards between Dolphins' zone coverage defenders. Detroit failed to pick up the next third-and-short when Goff's arm was hit by Dolphins defender Josh Uche.

That set up a fourth-and-3 from the Dolphins' 31-yard line. Detroit went for it, and Goff avoided pressure to find Isaac TeSlaa for 8 to keep the drive alive. Then Jahmyr Gibbs took a wildcat snap, faked a pitch to Goff, and took it for 16 yards down to the Dolphins' 6-yard line.

But on third-and-goal, Goff was sacked by Uche, forcing the Lions to settled for a chip-shot field goal. 3-0 Lions.

Detroit managed to get a quick three-and-out on defense after two rushes went for 0 yards, and Malik Willis' third-down pass was too far for his receiver.

But the Lions quickly gave the ball back to Miami. After two successful runs, Goff's arm was hit again by Uche while throwing, and the ball went right to Dolphins defensive back Chris Johnson.

Miami moved into scoring position with a leaping grab from Caleb Douglas for 20 yards down to the Lions' 20-yard line. In the red zone, the Dolphins faced a third-and-11 and they tried to catch Detroit sleeping with a draw play. But Aidan Hutchinson sniffed it out for a short gain, and the Dolphins settled for a field goal to tie it up. 3-3 tie.

The Lions offense gained just 3 yards on their first two plays to set up a big third-and-7 to start the second quarter.

On the first play, Goff went deep to Jameson Williams, but the receiver bobbled a very catchable ball and the Lions were forced to punt…. or were they?!? Jack Fox drilled a pass to Tay Martin for the fake punt conversion and 11 yards.

Detroit had to dig themselves out of hole, though, as Frazier was called for a holding penalty on the next play. While an 11-yard pass to St. Brown helped, a failed screen set up a third-and-9. And on the play, the Dolphins sent an aggressive blitz and Miami picked up their third sack of the game. This time, the Lions did actually punt the ball away.

The Dolphins were pinned at their own 5-yard line, but a play-action pass to Greg Dulcich for 11 yards got Miami out of the jam. That said, Hutchinson drew a holding penalty that eventually set up a third-and-18 for the Dolphins. Pressure from the Lions forced Willis to throw it away.

Despite a holding penalty on the Lions on the punt, they still got great field position due to a shank from Dolphins punter Bradley Pinion. Detroit started on their own 43-yard line, hoping to put some of the offensive line issues behind them. The drive started promisingly with an 11-yard pass to Sam LaPorta and a 10-yard run from Gibbs. Two plays later, Goff hit St. Brown for another 14 yards.

However, the drive stalled from there. A toss to Gibbs lost 3 yards. Then another Gibbs run lost another 3 yards. Goff scrambled on third down to make the field goal a little shorter, and Bates drilled a 40-yard field goal to make it 6-3 Lions with 3:30 left in the half.

Miami responded before the half ended. A reverse to Kevin Coleman earned 16 yards and put the Dolphins in Lions territory. Ollie Gordon then got Miami into field goal range with a pair of draws that went for 9 and 11 yards. Eventually, Miami drove down to the Lions' 10-yard line and had a shot at the end zone. But Hutchinson drew another holding penalty, forcing the Dolphins to kick a game-tying field goal, but former Lions Zane Gonzalez missed a 38-yard field goal to keep it 6-3 Lions at halftime.

Miami started with the ball and picked up a quick first down thanks to a pass interference penalty on Derrick Barnes. He made amends with a tackle for loss on the next play, helping set up a third-and-11 for the Dolphins. Willis tried to force a ball into a tight window, but safety Chuck Clark picked it off and returned it all the way to the Dolphins 26-yard line.

Gibbs gave the Lions a new set of downs inside the red zone with a third-and-1 conversion with a 3-yard gain on a toss. However, the Lions had to settle for another field goal when a second down Gibbs run went for no gain and Sam LaPorta committed a false start to set up a third-and-11. Goff turfed a pass to Gibbs, and Bates was good from 33. 9-3 Lions.

Bates' ensuing kickoff was well short of the landing zone, setting the Dolphins up at the 40-yard line. Miami turned that into points. One key play was a third-and-11 pass to Douglas, who ran a 9-yard curl, then avoided a tackle attempt from Ennis Rakestraw to get the first down. Detroit drew another holding penalty—Skyler Gill-Howard this time. And it forced Miami to settle for another field goal attempt. This time Gonzalez was good from 52 yards. 9-6 Lions.

Detroit looked to retaliate quickly. A 31-yard strike to Jameson Williams immediately put the Lions in field goal position on the first play of the drive.

Goff hit St. Brown for 17 on the very next play, putting Detroit into the red zone. The Lions then faced a third-and-1, and the Dolphins were all over Detroit's play-action attempt. The Lions obviously went for it on fourth-and-1, and Detroit dialed up a well-timed pitch to Gibbs, who beat everyone to the outside for an 8-yard touchdown. 16-6 Lions.

Miami faced a third-and-3 at the start of the fourth quarter.

The Dolphins failed to convert after Malcolm Rodriguez punched out the ball on what would've been a converted first down pass. But Miami pulled off a fake punt of their own, and it was even more successful than Detroit's, gaining 46 yards.

Then, on a third-and-5 inside the red zone, Willis found Malik Washington for 7 yards to move the chain. Alim McNeill tallied a sack to put the Dolphins in a tough third-and-goal situation from the 13.

Derrick Moore chased down Willis on third down, forcing yet another field goal from the Dolphins. 16-9 Lions.

Detroit avoided a third-and-out when an attempt to St. Brown drew a 17-yard pass interference penalty. That would be all the Lions could muster, though. A holding penalty on Blake Miller pushed the Lions back, but Detroit dug out of it with a 17-yard screen to St. Brown on a third-and-8.

Detroit would stall out from there, as Goff overthrew St. Brown on third-and-7. Bates' 43-yard field goal was good, to give Detroit a two-score lead with 4:28 left. 19-9 Lions.

Starting at their own 35-yard line, the Dolphins had to score twice and score quickly. But Detroit's defensive line took over. Hutchinson forced a throw away on first down, Moore got a sack on second down, and on fourth-and-12, the Dolphins dropped a potential conversion. Detroit took over at Miami's 33 with 3:02 left and the game in hand.

The Lions offense managed to earn a couple of first downs and bleed the rest of the clock to move to 6-2 on the season at the midway point of the year.

#2720. Final score: Kansas City Chiefs defeat New York Jets 35-12 in Week 9

The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 in Week 9 of the 2026 NFL regular season.

Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a beating in the game, but ended with an impressive stat line. The two-time MVP completed 23 of his 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns without being intercepted, and spent much of the game evading opposing defensive linemen.

Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III was the Chiefs' leading rusher with 102 yards on 18 carries, one of which scored a touchdown in the second half. Star sack-master Chris Jones tallied two sacks and four total tackles in a rebound performance.

#2718. Pavlović jokes about Kane's salary and explains why Mainz away is always difficult

Bayern managed to get a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Mainz 05 in an exciting Bundesliga encounter. Aleksandar Pavlović explained why Mainz remain a difficult opponent on home soil, pointing to their physical approach and direct style of play.

"I think it's because Mainz play a very unpleasant style of football. They play a lot of long balls and constantly look for second balls. They also try to win as many fouls as possible. That makes things difficult, but I think we dealt with it well today and deserved to win," he said.

The midfielder was also pleased to see Lennart Karl continue his impressive form despite the criticism surrounding the young forward.

"As a professional footballer, you simply have to be able to deal with things like that. I don't think he pays too much attention to what's going on outside. He just gets on with things and plays his football. I'm obviously delighted that he scored today as well," Pavlovic explained.

Regarding Vincent Kompany's potential return after the international break, the 21-year-old remained hopeful but stressed that the coach should take the time he needs.

"We'd all be delighted if he could return as soon as possible. But that's for the coach to decide. He should take as much time as he needs. Obviously, we'll be very happy when he's back."

Asked whether he had been in contact with Kompany recently, Pavlovic added: "Yeah, I saw him briefly once. That was about it."

There was also room for a joke when Kane's salary came up during the interview. Pavlovic responded with a grin: "Good thing you reminded me about his salary. I'll bring that up with him in the dressing room. Maybe he'll buy us the occasional coffee!"

#2716. Giants get first win in Philadelphia since 2013

Sunday's performance in Philadelphia wasn't a work of art for the Giants, but it was more than good enough to end their long losing streak in the City of Brotherly Love.

Tight end Isaiah Likely's touchdown catch in the third quarter gave the Giants their first lead since the first quarter and they expanded it to 19-11 before punting the ball back to the Eagles with 90 seconds left to play in the game. Joe Milton picked up first downs on completions to Hollywood Brown and Dallas Goedert, but rookie wideout Makai Lemon dropped a pass that would have moved them into Giants territory and running back Elijah Mitchell didn't get out of bounds on a short catch on the next play.

Milton spiked the ball with six seconds left to play and the Eagles on their own 44-yard-line for one final heave. Milton famously uncorked a 70-yard throw at the Combine, but he never got a chance to throw the ball because he was sacked by defensive end Darius Alexander.

That was one of seven Giants sacks on the afternoon, including three from first-round pick Arvell Reese. It was Reese's first road game against the Eagles and his 1-0 record in Philly is a big change from recent history. The Giants had lost 13 straight games in Philadelphia and the route to ending that skid featured some strange twists and turns.

Likely's touchdown catch came on a throw from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy after McCarthy hurt his hip in the third quarter. Winston played one full series and threw for 71 yards on his way to the touchdown, but McCarthy returned just before the end of the quarter and led the offense for the rest of the proceedings.

McCarthy was sacked five times, but was 12-of-19 for 127 yards when he had time to throw and he ran for 22 yards while evading pressure over the course of the afternoon. The Giants couldn't find any other success on the ground and Sunday's 243 yards of offense didn't make a strong case for the Giants sitting out the trade deadline if they have a chance to acquire any kind of help for their backfield.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers had five catches for 43 yards, but dropped a pass in the end zone that would have iced the win and his body language was that of an unhappy player throughout the game. The win should make it easier to avoid it being a focal point for the team after the game, but Nabers will likely have to answer some questions about what was bugging him.

They'll be back on the field Thursday night against the Commanders and another win would move them to 6-2-1 with a 3-0-1 record in the division. That would make them even heavier favorites to win an NFC East that is theirs for the taking.

The Eagles spent a lot of time in that position in recent years, but injuries have gutted the roster and Milton didn't provide any significant upgrade on the offensive production that the team got with Tanner McKee at quarterback. The Eagles will have a bye week to determine which way they want to go in the future, but the 2-7 team should really only have eyes on 2027 at this point.

#2714. I'm not going to rewrite last four years - DeChambeau on LIV

Bryson DeChambeau says he is "not going to rewrite the last four years" in his first public statement since the intention to wind down LIV Golf was confirmed, adding he "gave everything" to keep the tour alive.

The two-time US Open champion led a selection of stars in joining LIV four years ago and maintained his commitment even after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing for the breakaway tour in April.

DeChambeau said in May he was "working hard to find a solution" and then in August, when it was confirmed LIV's season would be ending early, the American suggested "something fun is coming".

"I'm not going to rewrite the last four years - I made a decision I believed in and I'm grateful for what came with it," wrote the 33-year-old in an Instagram post, referencing "record crowds" at LIV Golf events in Australia and South Africa.

"I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that and I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive."

LIV confirms intention to wind down after five years

DeChambeau proud of what LIV has achieved

DeChambeau denies 'completely untrue' PGA talks

LIV Golf this week confirmed its intention to wind down operations because of a lack of financial support.

That was followed by a number of high-profile players, including two-time major winner Jon Rahm and England's Lee Westwood, announcing their decision to quit the tour.

DeChambeau acknowledged his immediate future now lay elsewhere, confirming he will be playing in Gary Player's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa in December.

"Beyond that, I'll go about whatever is next in the right way," he said.

"Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help.

"Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.

"My passion has been to grow this game. That's still the goal."

LIV Golf, which promised its players huge fees and prize money, caused fissures to open up in the sport.

Rory McIlroy was one of its most high-profile detractors and this week said LIV had attempted to "destroy the European Tour".

DeChambeau, however, reiterated his commitment to the concept of team golf, which was central to LIV Golf, in which professionals were grouped together to compete for a team prize alongside individual honours.

"I still believe in team golf," added the captain of LIV's Crushers team, which included England's Paul Casey.

"It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game."

#2711. Cowboys rally late to avoid disaster vs. Colts after blowing lead, multiple second-half miscues

The Dallas Cowboys almost blew it for another tough loss on Sunday.

But they rallied for a late touchdown to secure a 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Dallas blew a 17-7 halftime lead and allowed the Colts to take a 23-20 advantage in the game's final two minutes. But it recovered for a game-winning touchdown drive in the final 1:37 set up by a big pass from Dak Prescott to Ryan Flournoy.

On the first play after a Colts go-ahead field goal, Prescott found Flournoy on a 46-yard deep ball into Indianapolis territory.

The play ultimately set up Javonte Williams for a one-yard go-ahead touchdown with 1:08 remaining.

A beleaguered Colts offense helmed by Daniel Jones didn't mount a response on its final possession. Jones threw an interception on third-and-22 to Caleb Downs that sealed the Dallas victory.

With the win, the Cowboys improved to 4-5 to remain afloat in what should be a wide-open race for the NFC East. The Giants beat the Eagles Sunday, 19-11, to improve to 5-2-1 and remain in control of the division.

The win for the Cowboys avoided potential disaster that was set up by multiple second-half mistakes.

The Dallas defense allowed the Colts to cut their deficit to 20-17 late in the third quarter on a 55-yard catch-and-run by Ashton Dulin that featured a missed tackle near the line of scrimmage.

The Cowboys looked poised to respond on their next possession on a wild play by CeeDee Lamb. But it ultimately resulted in a Cowboys turnover.

Lamb caught a deep ball down the right sideline into Colts territory. He wasn't touched down when he fell to the turf after making the catch, and he got and up and ran from the Indianapolis 39-yard line to inside the 15.

But Lamb fumbled on the ensuing tackle. He was initially ruled down on the field, but the Colts challenged. Replay showed that he lost control of the ball before going down.

And what looked like sure Dallas points ended up in a turnover.

But the Colts couldn't capitalize. After they drove into Dallas territory, Jonathan Taylor gave the ball back with a fumble of his own at the Dallas 20, and the Cowboys lead remained at 20-17.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Cowboys and Colts face off in Week 9.

It was a battle of the Downs brothers between Caleb Downs (Cowboys) and Josh Downs (Colts).

Caleb earned bragging rights on Sunday as he picked off Daniel Jones to seal the game for Dallas.

After the turnover, the Cowboys kneeled the clock out and secured the 27-23 win.

The Cowboys had little time to work with and made it down the field and into the end zone.

Dak Prescott flipped the field with a huge pass to Ryan Flournoy who had an impressive one-handed grab.

After a later DPI in the end zone on Flournoy, Javonte Williams got the carry at the goal line and the Colts let him into the end zone to maximize their time.

After the extra point, Dallas leads 27-23 with 1:08 left. Indy has two timeouts.

Indianapolis takes a 23-20 lead thanks to Spencer Shrader's 50-yard field goal.

The Cowboys have no timeouts, but will have 1:37 to work with as they need to at least score a field goal to avoid losing this game in regulation.

The Cowboys got into field goal range with a chance to take the lead late against the Colts.

Brandon Aubrey attempted the 50-yard field goal. The snap was mishandled briefly, but regardless, Aubrey got the kick off but pushed it wide left.

Indianapolis takes over on its own 40-yard line with 3:30 to go in regulation.

Indianapolis faced fourth and 4 at the Dallas 41-yard line.

Spencer Shrader nailed the 59-yard field goal to tie the game at 20 with just under 6 minutes left in regulation.

The Cowboys-Colts game has been crazy down the stretch.

After the crazy play where CeeDee Lamb took off for 48 yards after not being touched, but then fumbled, the Cowboys had a 40-yard DPI call to flip the field.

Dallas had another 15-yard penalty for unnecessary roughness that got the Colts to the red zone. Star running back Jonathan Taylor fumbled it, though, and the Cowboys recovered.

It looked like Dak Prescott managed to barely get the ball to CeeDee Lamb for a first down.

Despite a rookie Colts defender being right next to him, Lamb popped up and took off down the field.

He didn't appear touched and Lamb picked up 48 yards.

When he was tackled, it looked like he was down, but then he fumbled. Indianapolis challenged, and it was ruled a fumble and Colts ball.

Daniel Jones threw a short pass to Ashton Dulin near the sideline, but it is going to go in the books as a 55-yard touchdown.

Dulin, a former D-2 track star according to the broadcast, showed off his speed and took off down the sideline and all the way to the end zone.

Dallas now leads 20-17 with 1:17 left to go in the third quarter.

Dallas now leads 20-10 with about 2 minutes to go in the third quarter. The Cowboys ran 10 plays and picked up 60 yards.

On third and 8 on the Colts' 9-yard line, Dak Prescott tried to hit Ryan Flournoy, but the pass fell incomplete.

Brandon Aubrey easily knocked through the 28-yard field goal, though, to extend Dallas' lead to double digits.

Indianapolis finally sustained a drive for the first time since the first quarter.

The Colts ran 11 plays and picked up 29 yards. While it wasn't the longest drive, it got Indy into field goal range.

The Colts attempted a 47-yard field goal and made it. Cowboys still lead 17-10.

Halftime wasnt enough for Indianapolis to shake its offensive woes.

Daniel Jones found Jonathan Taylor for a gain of six, but then had back-to-back incompletions.

The Colts have already punted 6 times in this game and currently trail the Cowboys 17-7.

Dallas' offense has been terrible in the first half.

Finally, Dak Prescott sparked some life into the team. Ge hit CeeDee Lamb for a 22-yard gain.

The duo followed it up with a 44-yard touchdown pass.

All of a sudden Dallas leads 17-7 just before halftime.

Halftime is nearing and the Cowboys will have the chance to spark something before the break.

It looked like Dallas may have finally re-sparked its offense with Tyler Goodson picking up 12 yards on first down.

Goodson got the carry on the next play and picked up seven. He got stuffed for a one-yard loss, and then Dak Prescott had an incompletion leading to yet another Dallas punt in the first half.

Four consecutive drives in the game have ended in a punt.

The offenses have stalled in the Cowboys-Colts game.

Indianapolis' last two drives have been a 3-and-out and they sandwich Dallas' most recent drive which was also a 3-and-out.

Colts running back Seth McGowan has scored his first career TD.

Jonathan Taylor had lost his shoe the play before and he had to come off the field for the Colts' offense.

The Colts take a 7-3 lead with 6:13 left in the first quarter.

Dallas' second drive of the game ended before it could get going.

Dak Prescott was hit from behind and the ball popped out. Indianapolis recovered and took over in the red zone.

Despite the mounting pressure, he remained defiant following the latest setback at Selhurst Park. "It's not from the dream to the nightmare," the 47-year-old insisted. "I'm not feeling this. I'm just in my job, and focusing on my job, and what I have to do to find the solution. The results are not at this level, and I know I have to push more on those things, especially in our way of playing, to make that move."

A significant part of the problem appears to be a clash between Sage's preferred philosophy and the current profile of the squad. At Lens, Sage built a reputation for high-tempo pressing and dominance in possession, but the Eagles have struggled to replicate that intensity. The squad has missed the spark provided by Ismaila Sarr, whose absence through injury has been harshly felt after he scored 21 goals last season.

Sage has also been forced to deal with off-field distractions regarding the futures of Jean-Philippe Mateta and Sarr, both of whom have been linked with exits. This combination of bad luck and tactical misalignment has seen Palace winless in the league since mid-October. Reflecting on the current situation, the manager admitted the gap between their output and expectations. "We have to be more competitive," Sage explained to The media. "At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things, but we don't have the results expected."

With the international break providing a natural window for change, the Palace board is considering immediate alternatives. Along with Frank, former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche is also believed to have supporters within the club's leadership. Both managers are currently out of work, making them viable options to step in before the Eagles travel to face Coventry on November 21. The pressure is compounded by the fact that Sage's predecessor, Oliver Glasner, enjoyed immense success by delivering the club's first FA Cup and a Europa Conference League trophy before moving to Forest.

The current run of form, sparked by a humiliating 5-0 derby defeat to Brighton, has left Sage as the bookmakers' favorite to become the first managerial casualty of the Premier League season. While some behind the scenes have expressed sympathy due to the injury crisis and the loss of elite talent like Michael Olise and Marc Guehi over the past year, the reality of the league table is becoming impossible to ignore. If Palace are to avoid a season-long relegation battle, the board may feel they have no choice but to act swiftly before the festive period begins. The next two weeks will be decisive for Sage's future in South London.

#2706. Cowboys survive after wild CeeDee Lamb catch and fumble late in win over Colts

Luckily for the Dallas Cowboys, CeeDee Lamb's wild catch-turned-fumble late on Sunday afternoon didn't cost them the game at Lucas Oil Stadium.

The Cowboys beat the Indianapolis Colts 27-23 after a game-winning touchdown from Javonte Williams in the final two minutes. But it was a sequence with Lamb earlier in the fourth quarter that could have cost them the contest.

Lamb made an incredible catch in the fourth quarter, and managed to complete the grab while just barely staying in right up against the sideline. But instead of completing the play, Colts rookie cornerback Kenneth Harris didn't actually touch Lamb.

So Lamb jumped up and ended up making it all the way down 48 yards deep into Colts territory. But as Lamb was tackled, he actually lost the ball going down. That gave the ball right back to Indianapolis after a review.

It looked like that was going to cost Dallas the game, too. The Colts made it all the way down into scoring position, thanks to three major penalties — including a 40-yard pass interference call on DaRon Bland.

But inside the red zone, Quinnen Williams forced a huge fumble to give Dallas the ball right back and stop what would have been a go-ahead touchdown.

Eventually, it was Williams' touchdown that pushed Dallas ahead for good and gave it the four-point win.

Dak Prescott went 21-of-34 for 335 yards with two touchdowns in the win, which pushed the Cowboys to 4-5 on the season. They are in second in the NFC East race, behind only the New York Giants. Lamb had 195 yards and a touchdown on 10 catches. He found the end zone in the second quarter on a 44-yard catch.

The Cowboys will take on the San Francisco 49ers next week.

#2705. Blackhawks First Domino Falls With Soderblom Placed On Waivers

The Chicago Blackhawks wasted no time making the first of what could be a series of moves this week after returning home from last night's debacle in Carolina, capping off a nightmarish 0-3-0 Southeast road trip.

Backup goaltender Arvid Soderblom was placed on waivers Sunday afternoon, with all 31 other NHL teams having a chance to claim him and his contract, which carries a $2.75 million cap hit and expires at the end of this season.

If Soderblom clears waivers, he'll be assigned to the Rockford IceHogs in the AHL on Monday. Regardless, the Blackhawks will now look elsewhere for Spencer Knight's backup, with 2020 second-round pick Drew Commesso being the primary candidate to replace Soderblom.

Soderblom (CHI) & Poirier (WASH) on waivers

— Elliotte Friedman (@FriedgeHNIC) November 8, 2026

Commesso has patiently waited for his first full-time opportunity with the Blackhawks, serving as the IceHogs starter for the last three-plus years. The 24-year-old received a two-year contract extension this past summer after looking sharp in three spot starts in 2025-26 for the Blackhawks, going 2-1-0 with a .918 save percentage and one shutout.

It's been a mixed bag for Commesso so far this year with Rockford, with a 2-4-1 record and a .890 save percentage in his first seven appearances. However, he's been waiting in the wings for a while now, and the Blackhawks re-signed him this summer for a reason. It's time to give him an opportunity as the NHL backup.

For Soderblom, it's hard to say the development is surprising at this point, with an .885 career save percentage in 117 games for the Blackhawks since 2021-22. In his first five games this season, the 27-year-old Swede was 0-3-1 with a measly .842 save percentage and -6.1 goals saved above expected.

Soderblom is ranked among the NHL's worst goaltenders again early in 2026-27.

Worst Goaltenders – November 8 pic.twitter.com/TeXcTbax7d

— JFresh (@JFreshHockey) November 8, 2026

While the Blackhawks certainly have more glaring issues to solve than their backup goaltender, they have to start somewhere, and placing Soderblom on waivers is a warranted decision.

Without a reliable No. 2 option, Chicago has started Knight 14 times in 18 games. They've leaned on the 25-year-old heavily so far, and it's time to take some pressure off his shoulders.

We'll see on Monday whether Soderblom gets claimed off waivers or if he clears and reports to Rockford. The Blackhawks are scheduled to practice Monday morning, and it will be interesting to see whether Commesso will be with the NHL club.

#2704. Charles Bassey’s play is turning heads in Golden State

Every season I activate this trope to try and inspire a wary Dub Nation who wonders why we don't replace (insert suspect player) with someone else in the league. You're in the back seat of your mom's car, those sweet sweet Golden Arches come into view, and you make your pitch: "Mom, can we PLEAAASEEE get McDonald's?"

And without missing a beat, back comes the dreamcrushing sentence masquerading as a better suggestion: "We got McDonald's at home."

What's at home is never McDonald's, but it's ground beef, sandwich bread, ketchup, mustard, and relish. You eat it and more often than not depending on who your mama is, it hits. Your tastebuds are awash with flavor and gratitude. Maybe mom was right, maybe you do have McDonalds at home.

That's Charles Bassey for the Warriors right now. When Golden State asked for a real center, the front office looked at the cap sheet and injury report, and said, "we got a center at home."

And maybe the Warriors front office is right, maybe we DO have a big man at home!

And that is quite the development considering the hope of Kristaps Porziņģis dominating as the big man for the Warriors has effectively died as it looks like he's retiring from Warriors basketball. The team re-signed him this summer even though he'd missed 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams.

Then there's Al Horford, who is 40 years old and dealing with a body banged up from years of playoff warfare. Horford is a professional basketball genius. But asking him to play 30 minutes a night in November is not gonna have him available for any kinda playoff run in the spring.

And of course the Warriors can always counter with the grizzled, undersized legend Draymond Green at center. That works until Draymond does Draymond things and gets ejected two minutes into the third quarter, which brings us to the night the center at home showed up.

On Nov. 2 against the Suns, Golden State trailed by 17. Draymond had been thrown out for body slamming one Phoenix player and quasi strangling Dillon Brooks (rightfully so).

That's when Bassey had a career night, scoring 19 points on 7-of-10 shooting, grabbed 8 rebounds and finished +10. After Draymond's ejection, the Warriors outscored Phoenix 59-45. He also built a connection with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Four of Lendeborg's five assists that night went to Bassey. Every time the rookie lofted the ball near the rim, Bassey caught it and finished.

After the game, Bassey called out the Suns for "fake toughness." The center at home has a little seasoning on him, don't he?

This wasn't a one-night fluke. The Warriors started 0-3, then won seven straight to get to 7-3, and Bassey was in the middle of it:

He has a +34 plus-minus over the seven-game streak, and +33 in the five games where he played real minutes

His 15.7 rebounds per 36 minutes ranks second in the NBA

He's shooting 63.6% from the field and 88.2% from the line, with a 25.8 PER.

Over the streak he's averaging roughly 21 points, 15 rebounds and nearly 3 blocks per 36 minutes.

Ummm ladies and gentlemen, he's really balling in his role right now. Here's the case for more Bassey minutes: in the Orlando game, he played only 11. The Magic won the offensive rebounding battle 24-3 and outscored Golden State 33-2 on second-chance points. The Warriors still won in overtime, because Steph Curry is a supernatural force of nature on the basketball court.

Bassey isn't Porziņģis, a guy who stretches the floor to 28 feet or make anyone's All-Star ballot. He's 6-foot-9 and focused completely on rebounding, rim-running and blocked shots. He's also available to play, and we all know the best ability is availability.

Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy may still trade for a center; I absolutely think he should. Using Porziņģis' contract to match salaries for a real big makes sense, and they have a real chance to pull it off before the trade deadline.

Until then, Dub Nation asked for McDonald's and got told they had a center at home, and so far the one at home is providing a lot of sustenance.

#2698. Is Luka Dončić playing tonight? Injury update on Lakers star vs. Pistons

The Los Angeles Lakers are tasked with facing one of the NBA's best defenses in the Detroit Pistons in the first of their four-game road trip on Sunday, Nov. 8. They'll have the added challenge of doing so without the driving force of their offense.

Luka Dončić has been ruled out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Dončić was listed as questionable on Saturday, one day after the leading MVP candidate dropped a season-high 53 points at home against the Portland Trail Blazers.

It's a blow to the Lakers (8-2), who will be without Dončić's 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per night in nine games played this season. He's missed one other game with back tightness.

Detroit (6-2), meanwhile, has given up an average of 101.8 points per game, fewest in the league.

Amid Dončić's historic stretch of seven consecutive 35-plus point games, the last four of which he's scored at least 40, head coach JJ Redick was asked if there was any danger in relying too much on the two-time scoring champion.

"Part of planning and team building and playing an 82-game season is that you're constantly assessing and trying to be better," Redick said on Friday. "... Let's say you're running a nine-man rotation or 10-man rotation. It's rare that you have each guy playing great. The goal is for each guy to play great, but that just doesn't happen so you're constantly tending to things. It's just the NBA.

" ... We have to rely on Luka because he's our best player, just like every other team relies on their best player. We still have to coach everyone else and coach the team."

The Lakers could be choosing to be proactive with getting rest for Dončić, as they travel to Atlanta for the second night of a back-to-back on Monday.

Dončić does have a history of back injuries during his career. Before this season, he was most recently listed with a back injury in March 2025. He was also listed with back-related injuries during the 2019, 2021 and 2024 seasons.

Dončić entered his third season with the Lakers as the unquestioned leader. He was ranked No. 4 on USA TODAY Sports' top 100 player rankings ahead of the 2026-27 season and is currently No. 1 on Lorenzo Reyes' MVP power rankings.

The fatal flaw for the Los Angeles Rams might end up being that Nacua is all they have in the passing game.

Nacua was phenomenal again on Sunday in a grind-it-out 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. He had 14 catches for 150 yards on 19 targets with the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Nacua also ran it twice for 20 yards. Nobody else on the Rams had more than 20 yards receiving. Nacua had 150 yards and everyone else combined had 78. That's not an ideal formula, no matter how incredible Nacua is as a player.

The Rams weren't completely whole on Sunday. They played without cornerback Trent McDuffie and tight end Terrance Ferguson, among others. Davante Adams is out with a hamstring injury and could be out until late in the season, which is why the Rams have so few options at receiver. But they did have Myles Garrett back. And Garrett, like Nacua, was great. He had three sacks, including a big 12-yard sack with with the game still in doubt late in the fourth quarter. Los Angeles' defense held on, getting a stop on the final play in their own territory. The Rams still had key players out, but every team in the NFL is dealing with some injuries. The San Francisco 49ers, who lead the NFC West, can attest to that. The Rams just haven't been what everyone thought they would be yet, even though they are getting wins against overmatched teams.

But they are 5-4, which is why the trade deadline is very important for them. Los Angeles has already sold some of its future on trades for Garrett and McDuffie, and it's a team that probably needs another move or two to get back to the status of Super Bowl favorite. Particularly at receiver. Nacua needs some help.

In the third quarter Stafford forced a pass into Nacua despite Nacua being bracketed closely. Safety Nick Cross had an easy interception. It was a clear case of Stafford forcing it to his only receiver option, no matter what. It was Stafford's ninth interception this season, surpassing last year's total already. That type of play showed why the overreliance on Nacua in the passing game needs to be addressed.

It doesn't help that Stafford is dealing with an elbow injury. He has not been able to complete passes downfield in Los Angeles' past few games. It could be argued that the Rams having one option at receiver and playing three tight ends more than half of their plays is what's sapping the offense of its explosiveness, but Stafford's elbow doesn't help either. Their longest play on Sunday, against a bad Commanders defense, was 21 yards.

Perhaps Adams returns from a serious injury and fills the need the Rams have, but that's a gamble for a receiver who will turn 34 on Dec. 24. It also assumes Nacua, who has a long history of injuries and is taking a lot of punishment with all of the touches he's receiving, stays healthy all season. If Nacua goes down, the Rams' passing game will be in real trouble.

The Rams can celebrate their third straight win after a disappointing 2-4 start. But it's clear that they need to be making calls before Tuesday's trade deadline if they want to reach their peak this season.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 9 of the NFL season:

The Broncos and their good fortune: The Denver Broncos are catching every break this season. And they simply can't lose in one-score games.

The Broncos were trailing 14-13 and the Carolina Panthers had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line when they got one of the most fortunate interceptions you'll see, and it turned the game around. The Panthers decided to pass on first-and-goal and a pass that was heading for the ground was tipped in the air by tight end Tommy Tremble. Broncos safety Devon Key made a great play to realize the ball was still live and pluck it out of the air before it hit the ground. A challenge and a review showed it was a clean interception. That was a big turning point in a 26-21 Broncos win.

The Broncos got going after that. They scored two straight touchdowns to take a two-score lead. But Denver doesn't play easy games. The Panthers scored and then forced a punt after a pitch to Broncos running back Jonah Coleman was fumbled for a big loss. But Denver hit Bryce Young, who fumbled, and Denver recovered with 1:15 to go. It was another win for the Broncos in a one-score game, their 16th in a row in one-score games. That sets an NFL record which they tied last week when they held on in the final seconds against the Chiefs. The Broncos are 7-2, and piling up wins in close games. Per usual, they had some serendipity on their side.

Jameis Winston: Winston didn't start on Sunday but came up with the key drive the New York Giants needed to get past the Philadelphia Eagles.

Winston came in when J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game after taking a hard hit to his shoulder. Winston got one full drive and made it count. On the drive he completed 6-of-7 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown to Isaiah Likely. Winston also ran for 11 yards. Offense was a struggle for the Giants all game but Winston did his job. It was the Giants' only touchdown in a 19-11 win, their first road win at Philadelphia since 2013. They improved to 5-2-1.

Winston was benched for McCarthy as the Giants chase a division title in the terrible NFC East. But he might have been their most important player on Sunday, coming through when nothing else was working for New York's offense.

Kenneth Walker III: After a couple of quiet games against very good defenses, Walker got an easier assignment on Sunday. And he took advantage of it.

Walker scored two touchdowns on catches and another on the ground as the Chiefs' offense broke out in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets. He rushed for 102 yards and had another 41 receiving. It hadn't been easy for the Chiefs on the road against the Seahawks and Broncos the past two weeks, and Walker in particular was stymied. He was on a blistering pace early in the season but had just 105 rushing yards and no touchdowns the past two weeks. On Sunday he was back to his form of the first few weeks when he was getting buzz as a potential MVP candidate. The Chiefs are 6-2, and still very much in the mix for an AFC West title as long as Walker continues to play well.

Joe Burrow for MVP: The Atlanta Falcons were one of Burrow's toughest matchups in November. All he did was to 18 of 22 for 239 yards with two touchdown passes and one rushing TD. And that was just the first half.

Burrow's MVP push continued on Sunday in Madrid, Spain, as he threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. He probably could have put up even bigger numbers but the Bengals were up by double digits for most of the second half. The NFL Network broadcast repeatedly talked about how Burrow told them in production meetings how confident he feels and how healthy he is. It shows.

The Bengals are 6-2 and in good shape to win the AFC North, which is usually a prerequisite for winning MVP. He is putting up monster numbers. He hasn't won before and there will be some sentiment to recognize him with his first MVP award as he turns 30 years old. By the end of November he could be the clear favorite, though Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Caleb Williams are also in the race. But Burrow is looking like the league's MVP.

Malik Willis: The whole season is a tryout for Willis, who has to prove he's worthy of being the Miami Dolphins' quarterback of the future. Sunday wasn't a good day for him.

Facing a Detroit Lions defense that isn't good and was down multiple starters due to injury, the Dolphins never reached the end zone. Willis was inaccurate on many passes. The Lions were surprisingly quiet on offense too but it didn't matter. Miami couldn't score enough to keep up and lost 19-9. Willis was 13 of 25 for 128 yards and an interception against a Lions defense that was 29th in yards per game allowed coming in.

Willis has had some decent moments, and he has to be graded on a curve because of the lack of talent around him. But he wasn't good enough on Sunday.

Shedeur Sanders, but maybe Deshaun Watson: Sanders couldn't come up with the two-point conversion he needed to close out the win over the New Orleans Saints. But he might have given the Browns a reason to consider a quarterback change.

Sanders, who threw a go-ahead 64-yard touchdown to K.C. Concepcion late in the fourth quarter and also led a game-tying field goal drive in the final seconds of regulation, hit tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown in overtime after the New Orleans Saints scored first, with Fannin making a great play after the catch. But the Browns threw incomplete on the two-point conversion that would have won the game (there was also a holding call on the Browns) and the New Orleans Saints held on to a 23-22 win.

The loss stung but Sanders played well, as Watson sat out due to being in the concussion protocol during the week. Watson has mostly played poorly and the Browns have been winning in spite of it. Sanders had 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints with multiple clutch drives. It will at least be worth considering a change after that.

Sauce Gardner: Gardner's presence on the Indianapolis Colts is a constant reminder of the collapse of the franchise.

Last season, when the Colts were 7-2, Indianapolis traded two first-round picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell for Gardner, an elite cornerback. But Gardner has been mostly hurt with the Colts, who have fallen apart since the middle of last season. And on Sunday, with a chance to beat the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner got beat for the biggest play of the game.

Ryan Flournoy, playing a bigger role with George Pickens out, beat Gardner for a 46-yard catch late in the game when the Colts led 23-20. That set up a go-ahead rushing touchdown from Javonte Williams and the Cowboys defense closed out the win when rookie safety Caleb Downs picked off Daniel Jones, who had another rough day. Dallas held on for a 27-23 win.

The Colts' fall is far from Gardner's fault, but he hasn't helped and the Colts paid way too much for him. Him giving up the game-changing catch to Flournoy was just another reminder of how costly that trade was.

#2695. New York Giants vs. Philadelphia Eagles Player of the Game: Arvell Reese

The New York Giants needed their defense to deliver in Sunday's divisional matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, and rookie linebacker Arvell Reese answered the call.

Reese was the clear standout in New York's 19-11 victory at Lincoln Financial Field, delivering one of the most impactful performances of his young NFL career. The first-round pick consistently disrupted Philadelphia's offense, finishing with 12 tackles (10 solo), three sacks, three tackles for loss and a forced fumble.

His biggest play came in the second quarter, when he blitzed Joe Milton and delivered a crushing hit that knocked the ball loose. Linebacker Micah McFadden recovered the fumble, giving the Giants possession and preventing Philadelphia from building on its early lead.]

Reese wasn't finished there. He recorded another sack before halftime, helping New York keep the Eagles' offense in check. He then added his third sack in the fourth quarter, putting additional pressure on Milton as Philadelphia attempted to mount a comeback.

Philadelphia managed just 11 points, and Reese played a significant role in making life uncomfortable for Milton throughout the afternoon. His combination of speed, physicality, and pass-rushing ability gave the Eagles problems from the opening half through the final quarter.

The Giants have been searching for difference-makers on defense, and Reese is quickly establishing himself as one.

A three-sack performance against a division rival, highlighted by a momentum-changing forced fumble, makes this an easy decision.

#2693. Jameis Winston briefly takes over for injured J.J. McCarthy, leading Giants to 19-11 win over Eagles

J.J. McCarthy made his second start at quarterback for the New York Giants, but left the game with an injury in the third quarter. While he was being evaluated in the locker room, Jameis Winston led a touchdown drive to put the Giants ahead in an eventual 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

The victory improved the Giants' record to 5-2-1 and strengthened their first-place lead in the NFC East over the Dallas Cowboys.

New York's defense made Eagles QB Joe Milton III miserable, sacking him seven times. Making the first start of his NFL career, Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards and no touchdowns. The Giants also held Philadephia to 92 rushing yards.

McCarthy left the game after taking a hit to his right shoulder on a 3-yard run in the third quarter. He left the field without assistance and Jameis Winston took over at quarterback for the Giants.

After being checked in the medical tent, McCarthy attempted to warm up for a return to the game but grabbed his right side in pain and went to a knee. He subsequently went to the locker room and the Giants announced he was questionable to return with a hip injury.

Winston led the Giants to a touchdown on their next series, completing 6 of 7 passes and connecting with tight end Isaiah Likely for a 5-yard score. The big play on the 76-yard series was a 27-yard completion from Winston to Darnell Mooney that put the Giants in the red zone.

Accuracy has always been an issue for Milton, whose physical attributes continue to make him an intriguing prospect for coaches. However, his inaccuracy may have cost the Eagles a touchdown on a third-and-8 from the Giants' 34-yard line with 2:25 remaining in regulation.

Milton threw a pass low to Elijah Mitchell, who had to go to the turf for the catch. Had the ball been thrown chest-high, allowing Mitchell to run, he likely would have run in for a touchdown. Instead, he was short of the line to gain and Philadelphia had to settle for a 45-yard field goal from Jake Elliott.

The Giants initially took a 6-0 lead, finishing their first two possessions with Dominic Zvada field goals after J.J. McCarthy was sacked to stall each drive.

Philadelphia scored the game's first touchdown with Saquon Barkley scoring on a 3-yard run. That finished off a 58-yard drive highlighted by a 19-yard scramble by Joe Milton and a pass interference penalty on Giants cornerback Deonte Banks that resulted in 30 yards.

The Giants had only 88 total yards at halftime, due largely to five sacks by the Eagles' defense, two by Zack Baun. New York also managed only 16 yards rushing, with 8 of those coming from McCarthy.

Philadelphia didn't fare much better in the first half with Milton throwing for 87 yards and getting sacked three times. Additionally, Barkley was held to 22 yards rushing in 10 carries. Milton outrushed him with 24 yards.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Giants and Eagles face off for an NFC East showdown in Week 9.

New York has beaten the Eagles in Philadelphia for the first time since 2013.

The Giants' defense came up big on the Eagles' final drive as the New York defense's seventh sack of Joe Milton was enough to end the game, as the Eagles had no more timeouts.

The Eagles trail 19-11 with 1:56 left in the game after Philadelphia was able to get down the field and kick a field goal.

It was the Eagles first drive that didn't end in a turnover or a punt since Saquon Barkley's 3-yard rushing touchdown with 2:09 remaining in the first quarter.

JJ McCarthy got the ball to Malik Nabers in the end zone, but the wide receiver was unable to come down with it.

This set up a 38-yard field goal which was good.

New York now leads 16-8 with 9:06 left in the game.

Philadelphia turned the ball over on downs in the second quarter. Since then, the Eagles have had four consecutive three-and-outs, all resulting in punts.

Philly trails 13-8 at the end of the third quarter.

Jameis Winston is still in for injured quarterback JJ McCarthy who is questionable to return with a hip injury.

Winston led the offense down the field, picking up 76 yards. The drive ended as he found his tight end Isaiah Likely for the five-yard score.

Philadelphia's second drive of the second half, ended just like their first: with a punt.

Milton had three consecutive incomplete passes and the Eagles drive ended with the team not gaining a single yard.

Philly still leads 8-6 early in the third quarter.

Jameis Winston came in for a third down play as JJ McCarthy left the field after a big hit.

The Giants ended the drive with a punt, but all eyes were on McCarthy. When he went to the sideline, he attempted a pass and collapsed on the sideline grabbing for his side. He was taken into the blue medical tent.

The second half started with the Eagles getting whistled for a holding call.

After losing 10 yards, Joe Milton hit Makai Lemon for a six-yard gain, but then was sacked for a loss of 10.

Milton then took off for 12 yards, but it wasn't close to the 24 that he needed to get so the Eagles punted.

He was definitely helped by a favorable bounce and roll, but Eagles punter Braden Mann logged an 84-yard punt on Sunday against the Giants.

Mann was punting from his own end zone and the ball wound up on New York's 6-yard line.

The Eagles had the ball on the Giants 40-yard line. Nick Sirianni decided to go for it and gave the ball to Saquon Barkley. The running back was stuffed at the line and ended up losing a yard for the turnover on downs.

New York got the ball back, but had a three-yard pass, a sack for a loss of seven yards and a nine-yard run before punting for its fourth drive in a row.

Philly leads 8-6 with 30 seconds left in the half.

After logging two field goals on their first two drives, the Giants have had three consecutive 3-and-outs.

The most recent New York drive consisted of two penalties, a four-yard loss on a carry by Darnell Mooney, a sack of JJ McCarthy, and a completion to Isaiah Likely for a gain of 10, which set up fourth and 12.

Philly leads 8-6 with 4:47 to go before halftime.

After the Giants took over after recovering the fumble by Joe Milton, the offense stalled.

After a holding penalty, McCarthy hit Malachi Fields for a 10-yard gain. Then he was sacked before he found Devin Singletary for just a one-yard gain on third down, leading to a New York punt.

The Eagles lead 8-6 with 11 minutes left in the half.

Neither team wants to hold onto the ball.

After recovering a muffed punt by the Giants, Joe Milton took a huge sack from No. 5 pick, rookie Arvell Reese, and fumbled. New York recovered the ball, set up at the 50-yard line.

It looked like the Eagles were going to have a three-and-out. Philly punted after only picking up eight yards on three plays.

Giants WR Charlie Jones muffed the punt, though, and the Eagles recovered for a fresh set of downs and much better field position.

After punting on their first drive of the game, the Eagles are officially on the board. They were set up with solid field position to start the drive at their own 42-yard line.

Quarterback Joe Milton III connected with TE Dallas Goedert for 12 yards before putting up a 19-yard run, and three plays later, the Giants made a brutal error, committing a 30-yard pass interference penalty to set up the Eagles at the 3-yard line.

Saquon Barkley ran it in for his third career rushing touchdown against his former team.

The excitement didn't end there, however, as the Giants were penalized for too many men on the field on the extra point attempt, setting up the Eagles for a 2-point conversion — an attempt by quarterback Joe Milton right up the middle, which was successful.

New York increased its lead to 6-0 in the first quarter.

The Giants ran seven plays and picked up 23 yards after a Philadelphia penalty on its previous punt started them with better field position.

Malik Nabers came down with an impressive snag for 22 yards, while he was getting hit by a defender.

The Giants got down to the 31-yard line, but turned to Dominic Zvada for the 49-yard field goal which he made.

Philadelphia pivoted to Joe Milton under center for Sunday's game against New York. It is his first career start.

Milton couldn't get anything going on his first drive. It actually started with him having a false start on the Eagles' first play of the game.

Philly then had a three-yard run by Saquon Barkley, a five-yard completion from Milton to tight end Dallas Goedert and then an incomplete pass.

The Eagles punted back to New York with nine minutes to go in the first quarter.

New York got the ball first and picked up 45 yards on 10 plays. The drive was highlighted by J.J. McCarthy hitting Isiah Likely for a 27-yard gain down the sideline, and a 17-yard completion to Darnell Mooney.

After two incompletions and a sack, the Giants settled for a 53-yard field goal, which was made.

The New York Giants will be without top running back Cam Skattebo in Week 9, who's dealing with a hamstring injury suffered late in Week 7 ahead of the team's bye week. Expect Devin Singletary to be heavily involved in the offense without Skattebo and fellow running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. in the mix, who landed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.

#2692. Week 4 Look Ahead: Luka Dončić continues to dominate, while Kon Knueppel is back on the injury report

After Sunday's games, the 2026-27 NBA season will have completed its first three weeks. While devastating injuries dominated early on, historic performances have taken center stage more recently. San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama had a night rarely seen in NBA history, while Lakers star Luka Dončić is on an extreme heater. Let's look back at some of Week 3's key storylines and look ahead to what's to come in Week 4.

- Luka Dončić has been on a historic heater: With LeBron James no longer in the picture, the Lakers became Luka's "team" for those interested in that kind of conversation. And it also opened things up for him to do even more offensively, if that were even possible. Well, it was, and Dončić has been on a run rarely seen in NBA history.

Through nine games, the Lakers guard is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists, 1.7 steals and 5.8 three-pointers per game while shooting 49.8 percent from the field and 87.3 percent from the foul line. Sure, Dončić is also averaging 4.9 turnovers per game, but his overall production has minimized the impact on his fantasy value.

Not only has he scored at least 40 points in four straight games, but Luka has also tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds and five assists in each of his last seven appearances. At this rate, Dončić is well on his way to being the most valuable player in fantasy basketball...and possibly league MVP as well.

- Victor Wembanyama's historic night: Wembanyama's averages aren't on par with Luka's, but he's gotten off to the start that fantasy managers expected, based on his preseason ADP. The Spurs center had a huge night in the team's November 4 win over the Mavericks, tallying 52 points, 24 rebounds, two assists, two steals and eight blocks. Wembanyama joined Bob McAdoo as the only players in league history to finish a game with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks since blocked shots became an official stat.

Also, he joined Wilt Chamberlain as the only players to record at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and eight blocks. Wilt achieved that feat on five separate occasions in his storied career. With Wembanyama not turning 23 until January, this may not be the last time he records a stat line like the one he dropped on Wednesday.

- Kristaps Porziņģis stepping away from basketball: Unfortunately, the Porziņģis situation took another turn last week, as the 7-foot-3 center announced that he was stepping away from basketball. He's been dealing with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) since his time with the Celtics, and managing the illness has been a major challenge. Because of Porziņģis' absence, the Warriors have been withholding payment on his contract, and reports suggest the team hopes to trade him for a player who can help immediately.

For his part, Porziņģis said in a statement last week that he's willing to work with the Warriors to reach a solution that satisfies all parties. In his absence, the Warriors have relied more on Charles Bassey, whose contract won't be fully guaranteed until January 10. Undrafted rookie Graham Ike even made two starts early in the season, and Al Horford is providing bench depth.

- Yaxel Lendeborg is establishing himself as the early Rookie of the Year favorite: Porziņģis' absence was a factor in Golden State's three-game losing streak to start the season, but they've been on a roll ever since. Saturday's overtime win over the Magic extended the Warriors' win streak to seven, with Stephen Curry going off for 41 points on 13-of-19 shooting. The future Hall of Fame guard's big night isn't a surprise. However, Lendeborg has established himself, in the eyes of many, as the early favorite for Rookie of the Year.

During the Warriors' ongoing win streak, he has averaged 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.9 steals, 1.0 blocks and 2.1 three-pointers per game, shooting 53.0 percent from the field and 79.5 percent from the foul line. While many teams go young and bet on perceived upside in the draft, the Warriors prioritized adding a player who can help win now, with Curry and Draymond Green in the latter stages of their respective careers. Lendeborg does that, and he's also looked like a potential cornerstone in the post-Curry/Green era, whenever that may be.

- Kon Knueppel makes his season debut...and aggravates his hamstring strain: Injured just before the start of training camp, Knueppel made his first appearance of the season in the Hornets' November 4 loss to the Nets. Unfortunately, he played just under six minutes before aggravating his strained left hamstring and leaving. Knueppel didn't play in Charlotte's November 6 loss to the Celtics, and the Hornets have not provided a return timeline.

Making things worse for the Hornets, Brandon Miller left that game with groin tightness, and neither Moussa Diabaté (quad) nor Dennis Schröder (thigh) played against the Celtics. Naz Reid struggled the last time out, shooting 6-of-17 from the field, and his start in Charlotte has not gone as smoothly as many hoped. But with injuries, the Hornets will need more from Reid.

- Jalen Duren to miss at least two more weeks: The Pistons have been without their starting center since the second game of the season when he suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Duren's status was updated on Sunday, when the Pistons announced he's cleared to start on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

Paul Reed has filled in at center, averaging 12.8 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.2 blocks in 29.3 minutes per game. The Pistons don't need Reed to be a prolific scorer, but he has provided solid fantasy value as Duren's replacement. The disappointing part is that John Collins' production has dropped compared to his 2025-26 numbers with the Clippers. He's averaging 9.4 points and 5.9 rebounds per game and seems to be struggling to fully grasp his role in Detroit. The Pistons play three games next week, two against the Wizards, which could be a "get right" opportunity for Collins.

- Thunder reportedly acquire Nique Clifford: Needing depth due to their many injuries, Oklahoma City reportedly acquired Nique Clifford from the Kings for two future second-round picks. After a decent rookie season, Clifford fell out of the Kings' rotation, averaging 6.3 minutes per game this season. The move to Oklahoma City gives him a fresh start, and he's joining a franchise that has developed young players well in the past.

As for the Kings, will they look to add another guard? Kevin Porter Jr.'s name has come up before, and he's still a free agent. Whatever the Kings decide, one thing will remain the same: Darius Acuff Jr. will stay the focal point of their ongoing rebuild.

- The Wizards ended Week 3 without Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton: Davis missed the Wizards' final two games of the week with a sprained ankle, while Ayton exited Saturday's loss to the Thunder with a lower left leg injury. Alex Sarr played 28 minutes on Saturday, finishing with 15 points, 14 rebounds and one assist. He didn't record any defensive stats, but the third-year center has a higher ceiling when Davis is out.

Bilal Coulibaly started on Saturday and could retain that role, but he went scoreless on 0-of-8 shooting. The Wizards have a surplus of wings, which lends itself to smaller lineups for longer periods if Davis and Ayton can't play on Monday against the Pistons.

- The Nets and Timberwolves have light schedules: Brooklyn and Minnesota are the only teams scheduled to play two games in Week 4. However, the Timberwolves have a silver lining: both games are on light days (Thursday and Saturday). With those games against Dallas and Chicago, low-rostered options like Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland may be worth a roll of the dice for streaming purposes.

The Nets are also active on Saturday, but their first game is on Wednesday, the busiest day of the week. Nolan Traoré, who has been more productive than many expected before the season began, loses some luster in fantasy leagues because of the schedule. The lighter schedule helps Mikel Brown Jr., who isn't playing both games of back-to-backs because of the back injury that ended his lone college season early. Also, guard Egor Dëmin (leg) will be re-evaluated at the beginning of the week, and the schedule may open the door for him to return to action.

- The Mavericks will play on Saturday and Sunday: Dallas is the only team with games on Saturday and Sunday to close out Week 4. That means fantasy managers rostering Kyrie Irving have to anticipate him sitting out one of those games, at Cleveland (Saturday) and at Boston (Sunday). Caleb Martin started the most recent game Irving missed, a November 2 loss to the Kings, and accounted for five points and six rebounds in 21 minutes. Whether he starts or comes off the bench, Naji Marshall is a better streaming option than Martin on nights when Irving doesn't play.

#2690. Matchups that cost Colts in wild loss to Cowboys, including Sauce Gardner and Jonathan Taylor

INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts nearly pulled off an upset on Sunday.

Embattled and playing under the fires of trade speculation, Indianapolis fought its way back to take a 3-point lead late in the game ... only to have the defense give it back up, allowing a touchdown and a 27-23 Cowboys win.

Indianapolis (2-7) now turns its eyes to Tuesday's trade deadline, and how many players might be playing elsewhere next season.

Sauce Gardner is supposed to be the team's best cornerback, a shutdown player the Colts traded two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to get before the deadline last season.

And he was responsible for the play that ended up costing the Colts the game on Sunday. Gardner was put in 1-on-1 coverage against Ryan Flournoy, a sixth-round pick in 2024 who is playing a critical role only because Dallas did not have George Pickens.

Gardner had already escaped a bad highlight earlier in the game, failing to get his head around to look at the ball on a throw to CeeDee Lamb that only ended up being incomplete because Lamb didn't get both feet inbounds.

The veteran cornerback's ball skills have always been questioned, and he failed to find the ball on the most important throw of the game.

After the Colts took a late 23-20 lead on a Spencer Shrader field goal, Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott went deep in 1-on-1 coverage to Flournoy.

But he never got his head around, allowing Flournoy to haul in a 46-yard pass that gave Dallas a chance to play for the game-winning touchdown instead of a game-tying field goal.

Gardner was supposed to be the "prize" of the 2025 trade deadline.

Days before the 2026 deadline, Gardner showed why he wasn't worth the price the Colts paid to get him.

Lamb is the best Dallas player, the only high-powered weapon at Dak Prescott's disposal on a day when George Pickens was not available.

Indianapolis didn't do a great job of taking away Lamb on Sunday.

But the Pro Bowl-caliber wide receiver did a decent job of limiting his own impact.

Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown, bouncing back from a slow start to seemingly break the game open on an inexplicable Indianapolis coverage bust near the end of the first half.

Veteran cornerback Charvarius Ward appeared to pass Lamb off to strong safety Hunter Wohler, who's not an excellent coverage option, and a wide-open Lamb caught a 48-yard pass for a score.

He could have turned in an even bigger day, but Lamb was flagged twice for offensive pass interference for pushing off of Colts defenders.

Then he was involved in one of the weirdest plays of the NFL season so far. Under pressure on third-and-long, Prescott flung a wounded duck in the direction of Lamb on the sideline, and the receiver made a remarkable diving catch, grabbing the ball just before it hit the turf.

Indianapolis cornerback Kenneth Harris didn't touch Lamb down, and the alert Cowboys receiver got up and took off running for a 48-yard gain.

But Lamb wasn't able to hold onto the ball at the end of the run and he fumbled the ball away to Harris, erasing the play on a weird day for the Dallas wide receiver.

Taylor, the subject of so many trade rumors for weeks, seemed to have an excellent matchup on Sunday.

Dallas entered Sunday's game with the NFL's worst rush defense, a terrible unit that ranked dead-last in the league in yards and second-to-last in yards per carry.

Indianapolis struggled to run the ball instead. Perhaps still working through the loss of Quenton Nelson, the Colts had trouble controlling the line of scrimmage, and Taylor wasn't able to find much running room. Taylor ran the ball 13 times for just 46 yards, failing to break any runs longer than seven yards.

Taylor also made the game's biggest mistake.

Driving with a chance to take the lead, Taylor got swallowed by Quinnen Williams at the line of scrimmage and lost the ball, fumbling to take away a scoring opportunity.

Backup running back Seth McGowan had the two biggest running plays of the game, scoring a touchdown and ripping off a 36-yard gain later in the game.

An Indianapolis team that has struggled all season was always going to need some help against a Cowboys team that remains full of star power.

Dallas gave it to the Colts with terrible discipline.

The Cowboys were penalized 14 times for a whopping 153 yards, routinely putting themselves behind the sticks, wiping plays off the board and giving Indianapolis a chance to stay in the game despite another ugly performance from the offense.

For the most part, none of the calls — other than the two Lamb penalties, which seemed minor — were hard to understand. Dallas simply shot itself in the foot, repeatedly, allowing the Colts to hang around as long as possible.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Coltsall season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter.
